stages.name: Junior Software Engineer
stages.summary: Completes bounded work with clear goals and guidance, understands the user and intended outcome, verifies the output, and communicates promptly.

business-results.text: Clarifies the user, goal, and acceptance conditions before starting a task.
business-results.evidence: Can restate the user, intended change, and completion conditions.

business-results.text: Completes agreed work and promptly surfaces deviations that could affect the result.
business-results.evidence: Deliverable meets the agreement; risks or delays are raised early.

business-results.text: Uses AI only when permitted and suitable for the task; checks facts, code, and references in proportion to risk before submitting.
business-results.evidence: Can explain the change and show execution or manual review evidence.
business-results.applicability: Assess only when policy permits and the task is suitable for AI assistance; choosing not to use AI is not by itself negative evidence.

business-results.text: Checks acceptance and user feedback after delivery and follows up on unresolved issues.
business-results.evidence: Acceptance records connect feedback to follow-up changes.

domain-expertise.text: Applies foundational role knowledge to common tasks and asks for help when uncertain.
domain-expertise.evidence: Work passes basic checks and key concepts can be explained.

domain-expertise.text: Follows team quality, security, and privacy practices and checks edge cases before submission.
domain-expertise.evidence: Can identify obvious failure paths or sensitive-data risks.

domain-expertise.text: When AI use is permitted, provides useful context, judges whether the output fits the task, and explains when it should not be used.
domain-expertise.evidence: Changes include verification; generated content is not assumed correct.
domain-expertise.applicability: Depends on role policy, task risk, and available tools; sound decisions not to use AI count as valid evidence.

domain-expertise.text: Explains business objects, states, and data meaning in the task and checks normal and exceptional paths.
domain-expertise.evidence: Examples explain state transitions and data constraints.

domain-expertise.text: Uses reproduction, logs, and small experiments to diagnose routine problems and brings evidence when seeking help.
domain-expertise.evidence: Provides reproduction steps, eliminated hypotheses, and verification records.

team-influence.text: Communicates progress, blockers, and needed support clearly.
team-influence.evidence: Collaborators know the status in time to act.

team-influence.text: Uses review feedback to improve the work.
team-influence.evidence: Can explain why feedback was adopted or discussed.

team-influence.text: Works within role and authorization boundaries and escalates decisions beyond them.
team-influence.evidence: Does not make unauthorized commitments affecting others or users.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Turns feedback into a concrete improvement in the next task.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Fewer repeat issues or reuse of a new method on a related task.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Separates known facts, hypotheses, and unknowns when describing a problem.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: States what observations support a view and what remains unverified.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Represents contributions, mistakes, and risks honestly and closes owned work.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Corrects the record promptly and does not conceal issues or overstate results.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Sets small learning goals for current knowledge gaps and checks whether learning improves the work.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Learning goals connect to visible improvement in later work.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Describes difficulties after setbacks, seeks timely support, resumes progress, and recognizes unsustainable workload.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Explains support sought, recovery actions, and the outcome of another attempt.

stages.name: Software Engineer
stages.summary: Owns a feature or component end to end, delivers reliably, follows operational feedback, and supports peers when relevant to the role.

business-results.text: Owns delivery of a feature and tracks whether it solves the intended user problem.
business-results.evidence: Reviews adoption, completion, or user feedback after release and adjusts.

business-results.text: Makes evidence-based trade-offs among cost, quality, and speed within agreed goals.
business-results.evidence: Explains the choice, alternatives, and conditions that could change the result.

business-results.text: Where role policy permits and risk is controlled, compares AI with alternatives on total cost, quality, and risk while owning the user outcome.
business-results.evidence: Compares workflow time or quality and retains human review points.
business-results.applicability: Do not assess by AI usage frequency or speed; consider task suitability and available validation.

business-results.text: Breaks feature goals into milestones, acceptance measures, and pause conditions and updates them with feedback.
business-results.evidence: Plans include outcome hypotheses, dependencies, and changes.

domain-expertise.text: Designs a maintainable component solution and identifies interfaces, state, and major failure modes.
domain-expertise.evidence: Design supports requirements and explains capacity, migration, or rollback.

domain-expertise.text: Adds tests, observability, or security checks to important paths to reduce foreseeable failures.
domain-expertise.evidence: Tests or runtime signals demonstrate that key constraints are protected.

domain-expertise.text: When AI is used, validates generated or suggested work according to impact and risk; escalates or rejects what cannot be explained or verified.
domain-expertise.evidence: Evidence includes tests, comparison cases, reference checks, or human approval.
domain-expertise.applicability: Assess only when AI is actually used or the role is expected to evaluate AI output.

domain-expertise.text: Maps business rules into component data, states, and interfaces and plans compatibility and migration.
domain-expertise.evidence: The model explains exceptions, historical data, and migration checks.

domain-expertise.text: Tracks a component after release, rolls back or diagnoses failures, and verifies repairs.
domain-expertise.evidence: Release monitoring, rollback conditions, and verified repairs form a closed loop.

team-influence.text: Aligns dependencies and acceptance with product, design, and partner teams to deliver a feature.
team-influence.evidence: Decisions, dependencies, and owners are clear; changes are shared promptly.

team-influence.text: Helps peers avoid repeat problems through reviews, documentation, or sharing.
team-influence.evidence: Others reuse the practice; quality issues or handoff costs decline.

team-influence.text: Resolves collaboration disagreements by clarifying facts and constraints and reaching an actionable decision.
team-influence.evidence: The disagreement ends with a decision, owner, and review point.

team-influence.text: Preserves decision context, operating instructions, and known risks so peers can take over.
team-influence.evidence: A peer completes a change or diagnosis using the handoff material.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Changes the plan when evidence invalidates an assumption instead of defending the original approach.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Shows how new evidence changed priority or implementation.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Builds trust by keeping commitments, surfacing bad news early, and aligning expectations.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Partners can plan around updates and face fewer surprises.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Uses task fit, risk, and validation cost to decide when AI may assist, expert review is needed, automation should stop, or AI should not be used.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Identifies data, access, accuracy, or impact-scope risks.
human-competitive-advantage.applicability: Allows a context-based decision not to use AI.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Clarifies goals, constraints, and missing facts before choosing how to investigate an ambiguous problem.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Clarifying questions change the problem framing or investigation, with explicit limits to inference.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Adjusts methods, pace, or support after setbacks and tests improvement rather than repeating effort.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Explains concrete changes after failure and the next attempt's results.

stages.name: Senior Software Engineer
stages.summary: Clarifies ambiguous problems, weighs cross-component options, and drives project outcomes while making authority and decision boundaries explicit when proposing plans or pivots.

business-results.text: Turns an ambiguous request into a verifiable user or business outcome with baselines and guardrails.
business-results.evidence: The team can explain why, how success is measured, and when to stop or adjust.

business-results.text: Uses user evidence, market or operational constraints to align cross-functional teams on high-value work.
business-results.evidence: Priorities reflect opportunity cost and are revisited against outcomes.

business-results.text: Assesses contribution to outcomes and distinguishes causal evidence from correlation.
business-results.evidence: Explains metric definitions, observation window, guardrails, and attribution limits.

business-results.text: Proposes phased plans within the owned project or domain, connecting opportunities, outcome measures, investment, and work declined; quarterly is one possible review cadence.
business-results.evidence: The plan states outcome hypotheses, capacity constraints, and reprioritization triggers.

business-results.text: When results contradict the premise, reduces, stops, or redirects work within authority; beyond that authority, presents evidence and a recommendation to the decision owner.
business-results.evidence: Records include pre-set conditions, evidence, and where released resources went.

domain-expertise.text: Designs across component boundaries, balancing domain rules, system constraints, evolution cost, and reversibility.
domain-expertise.evidence: Proposal covers boundaries, trade-offs, migration/rollback, and failure paths.

domain-expertise.text: Validates the problem with users and product partners before choosing an implementation.
domain-expertise.evidence: Research, prototypes, experiments, or data narrow or invalidate an approach.

domain-expertise.text: Defines quality and security checks for high-impact solutions; where AI is involved, selects evaluation, human review, or non-use according to risk rather than treating adoption as a goal.
domain-expertise.evidence: Shows evaluation cases, monitoring/escalation conditions, privacy/access controls, or human handoff.
domain-expertise.applicability: The AI portion applies only when the solution or its risks involve AI; assess ordinary quality and security against the actual work.

domain-expertise.text: Sets a technical roadmap for the owned domain, balancing architecture, technical debt, and staged migration; includes AI investment only when relevant opportunities, risks, and validation conditions are clear.
domain-expertise.evidence: The roadmap includes dependencies, cost, risk, checkpoints, and exit options.
domain-expertise.applicability: AI investment applies only when the domain has a relevant opportunity or risk; a decision not to adopt based on value, total cost, and risk is valid.

domain-expertise.text: Evolves cross-component domain and data models while preserving definitions, compatibility, and historical meaning.
domain-expertise.evidence: Data meaning and migration correctness remain traceable after business-rule changes.

team-influence.text: Aligns multiple teams on goals, dependencies, and decision rights without relying on reporting authority.
team-influence.evidence: Produces an accepted plan, commitments, and escalation path.

team-influence.text: Raises team-wide quality through review standards, shared components, or operating mechanisms.
team-influence.evidence: Rework, incidents, or duplicated implementations decline, not just documentation volume.

team-influence.text: Helps peers take on larger problems through delegation with clear boundaries and feedback.
team-influence.evidence: Others deliver independently and reliance on personal rescue declines.

team-influence.text: Identifies capability gaps from project direction and recommends development, collaboration, borrowing, or hiring; authorized owners make staffing and resource decisions.
team-influence.evidence: Capability gaps connect to work risks, closing actions, and review periods.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Makes testable judgments under incomplete information and states confidence, risk, and disconfirming evidence.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Decision includes explicit assumptions and signals for reconsideration.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Understands partners’ goals and constraints and remains direct, respectful, and trustworthy through conflict.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Disagreements are discussable and commitments executable without avoiding hard issues.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Reviews outcomes and personal judgment to create learning that changes later behavior.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: A later project uses the changed mechanism and can explain its effect.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Asks questions that distinguish competing hypotheses and prioritizes evidence that could change the decision.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Explains which question ruled out which hypothesis and how the decision changed.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Recognizes systemic overload and capability limits under pressure, resets commitments, and supports team recovery.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Early risk reporting, scope changes, and recovery outcomes are traceable.

stages.name: Staff Software Engineer
stages.summary: Creates sustained professional value in a critical domain or across teams, scaling impact through reusable practices and collaboration without assuming company-wide governance or formal succession duties.

business-results.text: Translates domain-level business goals into sustainable product, technical, and operational outcomes.
business-results.evidence: Roadmap connects business measures, capability investment, and long-term cost.

business-results.text: When carrying relevant domain responsibility, contributes market, business-model, and long-term investment judgment across opportunities; company-wide portfolio authority is not assumed.
business-results.evidence: Decision states opportunity cost, downside scenarios, and evidence thresholds for further investment.

business-results.text: Establishes cross-team outcome reviews that shape priorities and subsequent investment.
business-results.evidence: Review shares definitions and attribution limits, assigns actions, and changes resource choices.

business-results.text: Translates annual direction into domain plans and quarterly checkpoints with dependencies and stop conditions.
business-results.evidence: Long-term goals connect to near-term investment through an adjustable plan.

business-results.text: Evaluates total cost and actual adoption for platform, reuse, or relevant AI investments, testing long-term value assumptions without treating adoption itself as success.
business-results.evidence: Compares maintenance, migration, adoption, and alternatives.
business-results.applicability: Assess the AI portion only when the investment includes AI or AI is an alternative.

domain-expertise.text: Sets evolvable domain architecture and professional standards while balancing product experience and engineering boundaries.
domain-expertise.evidence: Multiple teams adopt the approach and track quality, cost, and evolution outcomes.

domain-expertise.text: Builds quality evaluation proportionate to product risk; for AI systems, includes representative evaluations and regression monitoring.
domain-expertise.evidence: Reusable baselines, production monitoring, and clear human-intervention/rollback conditions exist.
domain-expertise.applicability: AI evaluation applies only to AI systems or risks within the actual responsibility.

domain-expertise.text: Identifies cross-team complexity or technical debt and makes the overall system simpler and more reliable.
domain-expertise.evidence: Consumers repeat less work and incidents, change cost, or complexity decline.

domain-expertise.text: Coordinates cross-team technical roadmaps, sequencing architecture, data, platform, and relevant AI work with compatibility boundaries.
domain-expertise.evidence: The roadmap explains cross-team dependencies, migration sequence, and acceptance standards.
domain-expertise.applicability: Include AI work when relevant to the opportunity or risk; when it is not relevant, explain the technical or product basis.

domain-expertise.text: Builds shared business semantics and data contracts across teams to prevent inconsistent local models.
domain-expertise.evidence: Key metrics, entities, and rules have owners and change mechanisms.

team-influence.text: Aligns and enables multiple teams through clear direction and shared decisions rather than personal approval.
team-influence.evidence: Cross-team leads make aligned decisions independently.

team-influence.text: Helps others take on more complex work through specialist coaching, review, shared assets, or delegation; multiple new owners or formal succession supply are optional evidence contingent on opportunity and authority.
team-influence.evidence: Multiple people can independently own critical areas.

team-influence.text: Improves team boundaries, collaboration, or decision mechanisms to remove recurring systemic blockers.
team-influence.evidence: Collaboration cycles or dependency risk improve sustainably and multiple teams adopt the mechanism.

team-influence.text: Works with management partners to identify domain capability gaps, knowledge diffusion needs, and key-person risks; headcount, hiring, and succession decisions depend on actual authority.
team-influence.evidence: Team capability plans support the domain roadmap and verify backup coverage.

team-influence.text: Drives adoption of cross-team practices by addressing migration cost and feedback beyond publishing standards.
team-influence.evidence: Adoption, resistance, and improvement are tracked over time.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Calibrates judgment on long-term uncertainty and knows when to invest, experiment, wait, or stop.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Across decisions, risk is calibrated and views update in time, not only explained after the fact.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Builds relationships across disciplines, locations, and interests where real disagreement is safe.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Partners share bad news early and engage in difficult trade-offs.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Updates judgments openly, incorporates outside evidence, and helps the organization revise its understanding.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Decision records preserve original assumptions and updates for later teams to reuse.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Uses external changes and cross-domain counterexamples to challenge established organizational assumptions.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Counterexamples lead to testable experiments or changes in direction.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Maintains evidence, risk boundaries, and truthful attribution under major delivery pressure and develops sustainable alternatives.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: High-pressure decisions record boundaries, alternatives, and accountable owners.

stages.name: Engineering Manager
stages.summary: Owns first-line management responsibilities for team outcomes, people development, collaboration, and operating mechanisms; understands the business and domain boundaries and uses professional judgment to review and delegate.

business-results.text: Defines team goals, outcome measures, and quality guardrails with partners and recalibrates priorities.
business-results.evidence: The team explains outcomes and trade-offs and adjusts based on evidence.

business-results.text: Allocates capacity across delivery, reliability, talent growth, and technical investment.
business-results.evidence: Allocation reflects business risk and outcomes, with trade-offs recorded.

business-results.text: Owns team outcomes and explains how management decisions contributed and where attribution is limited.
business-results.evidence: Distinguishes team delivery, external conditions, and personal contribution without appropriating credit.

business-results.text: Plans and reviews with business partners at the cadence the decisions require, linking user opportunities, team investment, and outcome validation; the cadence can change with context.
business-results.evidence: Plans trace to opportunity evidence, outcome measures, and resource allocation.

business-results.text: Renegotiates commitments when goals, capacity, or external conditions change, with clear accountability for scope cuts, deferral, or stopping.
business-results.evidence: Business partners acknowledge revised commitments and track their consequences.

domain-expertise.text: Understands the team’s business flow, key domain rules, and data definitions; reviews product, technical, and quality risks, engaging AI experts when relevant, without being measured by personal coding depth.
domain-expertise.evidence: Asks the right questions, involves appropriate experts, and owns the decision.
domain-expertise.applicability: Assess AI risk only when the team’s products, tools, or workflows involve AI.

domain-expertise.text: Builds testing, release, and incident-response practices proportionate to business risk; adds AI verification and human oversight when AI is used.
domain-expertise.evidence: Quality and recovery are measurable without excessive manager approval.
domain-expertise.applicability: Does not require AI adoption; when applicable, assess verification, fallback, and accountability.

domain-expertise.text: Enables product, design, and engineering to discover problems and validate outcomes end to end.
domain-expertise.evidence: The team tracks adoption and outcomes, not just on-time releases.

domain-expertise.text: Builds technical roadmaps with technical leads, allocating capacity, cost comparison, and risk validation for technical debt, architecture, and relevant AI options.
domain-expertise.evidence: Technical plans align with business cadence and have owners and staged validation.
domain-expertise.applicability: Include AI options based on business fit, total cost, quality, and risk.

team-influence.text: Builds capabilities for team goals through hiring, feedback, coaching, and performance management.
team-influence.evidence: Role gaps and growth goals are clear; performance decisions use sustained evidence.

team-influence.text: Designs clear goals, ownership, delegation, and decision mechanisms that reduce recurring friction.
team-influence.evidence: Issues are resolved at the right level and members have decision space.

team-influence.text: Manages cross-team commitments, conflict, and escalation so the team can focus on key outcomes.
team-influence.evidence: Partners accept priorities and escalation paths; conflicts do not remain unresolved.

team-influence.text: Plans team roles, capability gaps, hiring and development cadence, capacity, and leadership succession.
team-influence.evidence: Staffing supports business and technical plans, with succession measures for key roles.

team-influence.text: Addresses performance gaps and sustained overload through clear feedback, support, and review periods.
team-influence.evidence: Distinguishes goals, capability, motivation, and environment, with verified follow-up.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Makes people decisions from sustained, multi-source evidence while checking bias and uncertainty.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Can explain evidence, counterevidence, and follow-up observations.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Builds relationships where mistakes, risks, and disagreement can be discussed candidly while maintaining accountability.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Issues surface earlier and retrospectives use evidence.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Reviews whether management mechanisms produce intended outcomes and adjusts personal behavior.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Feedback and team signals lead to specific management changes and follow-up.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Uses explicit standards in promotion, performance, and resource decisions, manages conflicts of interest, and protects factual reporting.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Comparable cases use consistent criteria, with routes for appeal and correction.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Recognizes management blind spots and workload limits, seeks support, delegates, and restores judgment after setbacks.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Support and delegation reduce recurring firefighting, and decision quality recovers.

stages.name: Multi-team Engineering Leader
stages.summary: Within actual authority, leads managers to deliver across teams and is accountable for resource direction and organizational capability; strategy, budget, and reorganization authority depend on the role mandate.

business-results.text: Within organizational mandate, translates business direction into multi-team outcomes, portfolio priorities, and adjustable investment plans; executive strategy or budget authority is not assumed.
business-results.evidence: Team goals form a coherent portfolio and outcomes/resources are revisited regularly.

business-results.text: Makes organization-level trade-offs across growth, efficiency, reliability, safety, and long-term capability.
business-results.evidence: Names downside scenarios, risk owners, and conditions for changing course.

business-results.text: Establishes consistent outcome measurement and review so leaders adjust direction using evidence.
business-results.evidence: Cross-team measures are interpretable; attribution limits and misses are transparent.

business-results.text: Within actual authority, connects annual direction, phased portfolios, and recurring reviews while making assumptions, resource limits, and exit conditions explicit; cadence follows the decision cycle.
business-results.evidence: Planning horizons are traceable, and cross-team conflicts can trigger portfolio changes.

business-results.text: Stops ineffective investments when business direction or portfolio assumptions fail and manages resource shifts and team transitions.
business-results.evidence: Stopping and redirection include prior evidence, transition cost, and subsequent results.

domain-expertise.text: Ensures clear ownership and controls for critical technical, product, privacy, and security risks, adding proportionate evaluation and oversight when AI is involved.
domain-expertise.evidence: Critical risks have decision owners, monitoring, review, and response mechanisms.
domain-expertise.applicability: The AI governance portion applies only where the organization actually uses or provides AI.

domain-expertise.text: Sets cross-team quality and operational standards proportionate to business risk.
domain-expertise.evidence: Standards reduce incidents or regressions without unnecessary process burden.

domain-expertise.text: Engages experts on long-term domain and technical choices and understands business, user, and organizational consequences.
domain-expertise.evidence: Can compare paths and reversibility without substituting for specialists on details.

domain-expertise.text: Governs cross-domain technical roadmaps, connecting platform, architecture, and data investment to business direction, and evaluates AI investment and alternatives where relevant.
domain-expertise.evidence: The portfolio has expert review, dependency sequencing, and long-term maintenance ownership.
domain-expertise.applicability: AI project count or adoption is not a goal; explain the basis for adopting, declining, or deferring it.

team-influence.text: Within actual authority, hires, coaches, and evaluates managers and establishes management calibration and leadership handoff practices; organizational scale and succession outcomes depend on opportunity and mandate.
team-influence.evidence: Managers independently own team results and grow the next layer of leaders.

team-influence.text: Adapts organizational boundaries, decision rights, and collaboration to business and architecture changes.
team-influence.evidence: Reduces structural dependencies and local optimization; ownership and resources match goals.

team-influence.text: Builds organization-wide mechanisms for strategic communication, conflict resolution, and decisions.
team-influence.evidence: Key trade-offs have clear decision owners and teams understand shared direction and limits.

team-influence.text: Plans organizational capability, key roles, and management spans with relevant decision-makers; headcount, budget, and formal succession decisions depend on actual authority.
team-influence.evidence: Organizational plans support the business portfolio and review capability gaps against outcomes.

team-influence.text: Leads reorganizations, leadership handoffs, and resource contraction while maintaining delivery and testing new accountabilities.
team-influence.evidence: Transitions include communication, handoffs, risk protection, and organizational review.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Makes careful decisions under high uncertainty and competing interests, owning consequences and correction.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Decisions account for long-term risk, ethics, and counterevidence, not only short-term metrics.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Builds organizational trust and candor so information travels upward and bad news surfaces early.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Risks from different levels reach decisions and commitments remain transparent.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Turns reviews and external change into organizational capability renewal rather than one-off action items.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Practices evolve with evidence and learning transfers across teams.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Builds independent feedback and checks on major people and resource decisions to prevent concentrated information and interests.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Escalation, dissent, and correction mechanisms are demonstrably usable.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Maintains truthful information and decision quality through major failure or prolonged crisis and rebuilds organizational recovery capacity.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Crisis reviews explain recovery pacing, support arrangements, and mechanism changes.
